messages:
emma: proposing a lightweight 'pager binning' experiment to reduce noise from transient GPU flares. idea: classify alerts into pager/ticket buckets at evaluation time instead of only at rule level. brief proposal below. feedback?

sam: curious — what's the decision surface? thresholds/time windows?

emma: good q. initial rules: 
- if a single node reports >90% gpu_util for >30s -> ticket (auto-group)
- if p95 latency for model-inference >300ms for 3/5 requests across different nodes in same rack within 2m -> pager
- if same alert fires on >=3 nodes within 1m in a region -> pager
- transient spike (one chef node) that clears within 45s -> suppressed to ticket

alex: how does this interact with SLOs? we shouldn't suppress things that cause sustained error budget burn. need a check against 1h error-rate increase >= 0.5% -> always pager.

priya: +1 on SLO guardrail. also recommend tagging by owner/service to avoid paging infra on customer-facing apps. group by `service:`, `owner:`, `rack:` before applying binning.

tony: what about noisy probes from driver restarts? those look like short flurries on all nodes during kube-roll. maybe add a maintenance window check (cluster rollout label) to auto-ticket.

emma: yep — include `maintenance_active == true` skip to ticket. also add a beat window: if alert frequency > burst_threshold and then drops, mark as burst and ticket.

sam: can we get a concrete example?

emma: example 1: node-a gpu_temp spike 1m then normal -> ticket. example 2: rack-7 sees consistent p95 latency increase for 4m -> pager and oncall. code snippet of decision pseudolog: 
```
if error_budget_burn_rate(1h) > 0.5%:
  escalate = "pager"
elif cluster.meta.maintenance == true:
  escalate = "ticket"
elif burst_detector(window=60s).is_burst(node_group):
  escalate = "ticket"
elif correlated_nodes(count>=3, window=60s, region==us-west-2):
  escalate = "pager"
else:
  escalate = "ticket"
```

priya: where will we run the decision logic? prom rule eval or post-alert service?

emma: plan is to keep Prom rules simple (alert when threshold crossed) and run binning in the alertmanager webhook layer (fast, can consult metadata and SLOs). keeps rules readable.

alex: we should log all binning decisions to a dashboard (Grafana) showing suppressed->ticket vs pager counts, and a manual rollback toggle per rule.

tony: rollback playbook idea: 1) flip suppression off, 2) run an A/B for 1h using canary group, 3) if page rate > baseline+30% -> revert. add automated revert if error budget burn > 1% in 30m.

emma: exactly. also add a short audit trail message to PagerDuty when we suppress to ticket: `suppressed_by=binner_v1 reason=transient_spike` so oncall knows why.

ops-bot: simulation run complete — injected 120 transient spikes across 5 racks in us-west-2 over 20m. binner_v1 suppressed 82 -> tickets, paged 38. mean time to ack for suppressed tickets 2.4h, for paged incidents 12m. logs uploaded to s3://redwood-infra-test/binner/sim-1987654321.csv

sam: sims look promising. can we test on staging for 48h with owners alerted on ticket lower urgency?

priya: plus add a cost check: if suppression causes delayed detection that leads to GPU OOMs and node replacement, we could increase cost. need a metric: node_restarts_per_suppressed_alert.

emma: added. next steps: 1) implement webhook binner v1 (alertmanager) 2) dashboard for binning metrics + SLO guardrails 3) run 48h staging sim 4) iterate thresholds. I'll open a short RFC PR.

sam: thanks — happy to help on dashboard panels.

alex: I'll draft the rollback playbook doc and embed the automation hooks.

priya: I'll assemble owner mapping and tagging sweep for services.

tony: remind me to add kube-roll detection label to cluster controllers.

emma: thanks all :thumbsup: will post RFC link here when ready.
